deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page studies an arrangement of three pseudo-lines (D_i), i in I with |I| = 3, in the projective plane. Its double cover on the sphere is the combinatorial octahedron Õ, and the arrangement itself is the 'cube/octahedron' map C/O of the previous pages. Grothendieck works throughout with 2-element sets, i.e. torsors under Z/2 (mu_2-torsors). ∧ is their contracted product (the tensor product of Z/2-torsors), and 1 is the trivial torsor. The set Φ_i ≃ Φ_i^{-1}, so Φ∧Φ ≃ 1. or(I) is the set of the two cyclic orders on I. The previous page established two facts. First, an orientation of C or O is equivalent to an isomorphism (6 bis): (∧_i Φ_i) ∧ or(I) ≃ 1, i.e. ∧_i Φ_i ≃ or(I). Second, the two sides of D_i correspond to A_i = ∧_{α≠i} Φ_α = Isom(Φ_j, Φ_k).

This page continues the bookkeeping.
(8) The two vertices on D_i are D_i∩D_j and D_i∩D_k, so S_i ≃ I∖{i}.
(9) D_i, with its two vertices and two edges, is a bigon (a 2-cycle). The set of its flags is S_i × A_i, and the orientations are the flags modulo simultaneous flip. Hence the orientation torsor is Ω_i ≃ S_i ∧ A_i = (I∖{i}) ∧ ∧_{α≠i} Φ_α. Two rewritings follow. Using (6 bis), ∧_{α≠i} Φ_α ≃ Φ_i ∧ or(I). Using the canonical iso below, this gives Ω_i ≃ Φ_i ∧ ∧_{α≠i}(I∖{α}).
(10) ∧_i A_i = ∧_{α≠i} Φ_α = ∧_α Φ_α^2 ≃ 1 canonically, since each Φ_α occurs twice.
(11) Hence ∧_i Ω_i ≃ ∧_i S_i ≃ ∧_i (I∖{i}) ≃ or(I). The last iso is canonical for a 3-element set. A cyclic order i→j→k orders each complement I∖{i} by 'successor of i first'. Reversing the cyclic order flips all three, an odd number of flips, so the map or(I) → ∧_i(I∖{i}) is Z/2-equivariant.
NB. Start instead from an abstract family of three bigons (S_i, A_i). Then giving an iso (10) ∧A_i ≃ 1 is equivalent to giving φ: ∧Ω_i ≃ ∧S_i. When S_i = I∖{i}, this amounts to (11 bis) ∧_i Ω_i ≃ or(I), or equivalently (12) (∧_i Ω_i) ∧ or(I) ≃ 1.

What it serves. The next page reads (12) as follows: the three line-orientation torsors Ω_i determine a circle and an orientation of it. It also gives the mutual determination of Ω_i and Φ_i (13)-(14), which leads to a Proposition. That Proposition reconstructs the octahedral map from torsor data, with orientations of the arrangement corresponding to trivialisations. In modern terms this is a canonical, torsor-valued description of the orientation (chirotope) data of the rank-3 uniform oriented matroid on 3 elements, i.e. 3 pseudolines.
errors: No mathematical error found. The two rewritings of Ω_i in (9) are mutually consistent: (I∖{i}) ∧ or(I) ≃ ∧_{α≠i}(I∖{α}) follows from (11).
Minor gap: the identification of the 'two sides of D_i' (defined in Õ) with the edge-set of the bigon D_i in the projective plane is used implicitly in Ω_i ≃ S_i∧A_i.

ideas.what: Orientation torsor of a bigon (2-cycle) as the contracted product of its vertex-set and edge-set torsors, Ω = S ∧ A.
ideas.modern_name: orientation torsor of a cell complex / flags modulo flip
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (combinatorial maps, flag description of orientations)
ideas.where_published: Combinatorial maps/flags appear in Esquisse d'un programme (cartes); not this specific formula

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism ∧_{i∈I}(I∖{i}) ≃ or(I) for a 3-element set I.
ideas.modern_name: sign/orientation torsor of a finite set (determinant of a 3-set); parity argument

ideas.what: Encoding the orientation data of an arrangement of three pseudolines (equivalently the octahedron double cover) via Z/2-torsor identities (10)-(12), with orientation equivalent to a trivialisation of (∧Ω_i)∧or(I).
ideas.modern_name: chirotope / orientation of a rank-3 oriented matroid, expressed torsor-theoretically
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroids: Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence (1978); pseudoline arrangements: Levi, Ringel, Goodman–Pollack

missed.claim: A coordinate-free, torsor-valued (mu_2-torsor) formalism for orientation data of pseudoline arrangements. It replaces sign-valued chirotopes by canonical isomorphisms of Z/2-torsors, so orientation reversal and relabeling become functorial. The page only treats the trivial case of 3 pseudolines.
missed.quote: la donnée d'une isom. (10) équivaut à celle d'une isom. φ (11) ... se réduit à une isom. (11 bis) ∧Ω_i ≃ or(I)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A functorial (stack-like) treatment of chirotopes as torsor data is not standard in oriented-matroid literature, but this instance is elementary. Its interest is mainly as a window on Grothendieck's approach to the pseudo-line project.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct bookkeeping of Z/2-torsors for the 3-pseudoline (octahedron) case. It is characteristic of Grothendieck's canonical-isomorphism style, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The symbol written φ_α in (9)-(10) is the same script letter as Φ_α of the previous page (and 𝔏_i of the next page); it should be read consistently as Φ.
In the NB, the first word 'Quand' is struck out; read 'NB [-Quand-] on part d'une famille de trois bigônes (S_i, A_i)_{i∈I}'.
In (11), the bracket '[ ≃ ∧(I∖{i}) ⇐ or(I)' carries the marginal note 'isom. can. évident associé à l'ensemble à 3 éléments I'.
The '(10)' at the start of the line after the NB is a reference label ('iso (10) équivaut à celle d'une iso φ (11)'), not a new equation.
The small 'i' above ∧ in (11 bis) and (12) appears to be a mark/annotation, not an index.
